subject: Control decomposition and continuous verification plan - Acme Financial
messages:
From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@acme-fin.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-fin.com>, Sara Kline <sara.kline@acme-fin.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: control mapping + verification approach for RFP

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our RFP evaluation we need a concise technical appendix that maps your platform controls to our regulatory expectations. Specifically:

1) A controls decomposition mapped to NIST AI RMF functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and the EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems.
2) A description of your continuous verification / regression approach (how you detect drift, how often you run regressions, sampling strategy, and rollback triggers).
3) Any evidence we can attach to the RFP (sample test reports, SLA excerpt, and the regression harness spec).

Can you provide a single document that we can include with the RFP by end of day Thursday (2026-06-24)? Also confirm any blockers for redaction or IP-sensitive details.

Appreciate it — we’re aiming to move to short list by July.

— Alex
Alex Tran
Head of AI Procurement
Acme Financial Services

Subject: Re: Request: control mapping + verification approach for RFP

Alex —

Attached is a draft mapping and the high-level verification summary (we’ve left granular implementation notes redacted). Highlights below — pulling from the attached "RI-Control-Mapping-v1.3.pdf":

Control decomposition (short):
- Governance (NIST "Govern"): policy registry, role-based access controls (RBAC) for model deployments, approval gates for model onboarding, documented model cards and usage contracts. EU AI Act equivalence: transparency obligations + conformity assessment readiness.
- Risk mapping (NIST "Map"): automated asset inventory, model metadata catalog, high-risk tagging workflow, and context-aware risk scoring. EU: identification and classification steps for high-risk ML systems.
- Performance & monitoring (NIST "Measure"): token-level latency/cost telemetry, quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE for gen baselines, semantic similarity, calibrated confidence scores), and drift detection hooks (score distribution checks, representation skew). EU: performance monitoring for safety/accuracy requirements.
- Operational controls (NIST "Manage"): continuous regression harness (see attached spec), canary rollouts with automatic rollback, KV and prefix caching policies for reproducibility, and audit logs (immutable request/response traces). EU: logging/auditability for post-market monitoring.

Continuous verification and regression approach (summary):
- Cadence: weekly automated smoke regressions for critical prompt sets; nightly lightweight sampling for production traffic; full regression + re-eval on major model releases or quantization changes.
- Sampling: stratified sampling across business routes, customer segments, and token-length buckets; manually curated challenge sets for safety/guardrails.
- Detection: multi-signal anomaly detector combining model-score shifts, downstream metric degradation (CTR/acceptance in customer apps), and semantic drift via embedding clustering.
- Rollback triggers: thresholded decline in primary metric (customer-defined), spike in safety violation rate, or regression test failures above tolerances. Canary auto-fallback to lower-latency/qualified variant allowed.

Evidence bundle (what we attach):
- Regression harness spec (regression-harness-spec.xlsx) — includes test definitions, thresholds, sampling algorithm description.
- Example regression report (redacted) — summary of recent full-run results.
- SLA excerpt (SLA-excerpt-Acme.pdf) — uptime/backups/data retention bullets.

Open items:
- Confirm whether Acme wants raw test logs included in the appendix (we can provide redacted CSVs) or only summary PDFs.
- Sara from legal: if there are any log redaction requirements we should follow your template.

If that outline looks good I’ll finalize language and attach the artifacts for Thursday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.inference
To: marissa_cole@redwood.inference, Alex Tran <alex.tran@acme-fin.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.inference
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.inference
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control mapping + verification approach for RFP

Alex / team —

Attaching the technical regression spec (regression-harness-spec.xlsx) and a short readme with reproducibility notes. Summary of key technical design choices included in the spec:

- Test design: combination of deterministic unit tests (tokenization, logits sanity), synthetic adversarial cases, curated prompt evaluation suites, and holdout production-sampled traces.
- Metrics: primary metric is task-specific (accuracy or semantic-similarity depending on route); secondary metrics include response-time percentiles, safety-tag rate, and hallucination score (ensemble disagreement).
- Sampling algorithm: stratified random sampling with reservoir sampling for long-tail sessions; deterministic seeding for replay. We cap nightly sample volume to avoid PII exposure in artifacts; full-run exports are redacted.
- Regression orchestration: runs on dedicated infra with versioned artifacts (model hash, tokenizer hash, quantization profile). Every run produces an immutable report and an artifact bundle we can share as part of an audit.
- Acceptance gates: configurable thresholds per-route; we tag run outcomes as pass/warn/fail and surface via our Console dashboards and alerting.

Practical notes for Acme:
- If you want example CSVs from a redacted production replay, we can provide a limited sample set under an NDA addendum.
- We recommend adding an agreed rolling baseline window (e.g., 30-day baseline) for drift comparisons to avoid noisy short-term changes.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Applied ML Lead, Redwood Inference
